trend.title: Texas Troubled CRE Loans Fall Below $600M in November, but Nine of 33 Auction Listings Are Repeats
trend.scope: Texas (Houston, Dallas-Fort Worth, Austin, San Antonio) foreclosure auction listings
trend.metric: Under $600M in November Texas CRE foreclosure listings (headline: $560M), down from over $1B in October; 33 properties, 13 in Harris County
trend.summary: The Real Deal's monthly Texas distress report, based on Roddy's Foreclosure Listing Service, shows troubled CRE loans posted for foreclosure falling below $600 million in November after topping $1 billion in October. Thirty-three properties are flagged, 13 of them in Harris County, and nine are repeat listings carried over from earlier months. The largest new loan is a $56.7 million Goldman Sachs loan on Houston's Offices at Pin Oak Park (Norvin Healthcare Properties), about 10% of the total. Other new listings include Rastegar Property Company's Velo Flats in Austin ($11.3 million Thrive Lending loan) and Harris Investment Group's 106-unit Legacy Lofts in Dallas ($8.4 million Lima One loan).
trend.significance: Texas's fast non-judicial foreclosure process compresses disputes into the days before sale, producing restraining-order requests, notice and acceleration challenges, and claims that a lender agreed to forbear and then posted anyway. Repeat listings often reflect ongoing negotiations or litigation, and post-sale guarantor, recourse carve-out and deficiency claims commonly follow. Out-of-state syndicators, bridge lenders and owners of properties with housing finance corporation structures should expect contested workouts.

verification.quote: Texas distress report: Troubled CRE loans drop to $560M in November

verification.claim: Below $600M after topping $1B in October; largest new loan is 10% of the total; 9 repeat loans
verification.quote: The $56.7 million debt on the property makes up 10 percent of the value of troubled loans this month, which dropped below $600 million after topping $1 billion in October, according to Roddy’s Foreclosure Listing Service. That figure includes 9 loans that were previously flagged for foreclosure and rolled over to November.
Of the 33 properties flagged for auctions, 13 were in Harris County, home to Houston, the most commercial foreclosures of the counties included.

verification.claim: Pin Oak Park: Norvin, Goldman Sachs $56.7M
verification.quote: Norvin Healthcare Properties, which is based in New York, is facing foreclosure on the Offices at Pin Oak Park. Goldman Sachs provided the $56.7 million loan for the five-building medical office complex
Ari Rastegar’s Rastegar Property Company is facing foreclosure on Velo Flats, a 70-unit apartment complex at 2606 Wheless Lane in Austin. Thrive Lending provided the $11.3 million loan in 2022.

verification.claim: Legacy Lofts: Harris Investment Group, 106 units, Lima One $8.4M
verification.quote: Harris Investment Group, based in Orem, Utah, risks losing control of Legacy Lofts, a 106-unit complex at 2600 Highland Road in Dallas. Lima One provided the $8.4 million loan for the property.

verification.claim: Nine repeat listings; negotiations or litigation
verification.quote: Of this month’s distressed loans, nine have been flagged for foreclosure sales multiple times, sometimes reflecting continued lender negotiations or ongoing litigation.
The property is a beneficiary of the notorious “traveling” housing finance corporation loophole.
